name: equal-weight-rebalance-10m-threshold-015
rationale: Cost-side hypothesis (the 500k static-mix deficit has been negative for 21 consecutive runs; fee drag 5.79% explained ~43% of it on 2026-10-28). On top of equal weights + 600s spacing, raise allocation_threshold 0.10 -> 0.15 so small target moves no longer trigger a rebalance. Caveat recorded up front: at 50,000 JPY every threshold below ~0.25 is inert under the lot floor (doc 'Evaluation capital'), so a 50k result identical to equal-weight-10m is expected and is not evidence. The 500k/5M diagnostics carry the information. Score on total_fees_jpy, not trade count. The agent should also run equal-weight-10m at threshold 0.10 on today's window as an unregistered reference.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), set TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT from 0.25 to 1.0 (REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT stays 1.0), exactly as experiment/equal-weight-rebalance-10m-current-config (93e22ce) does. Nothing else in the function changes. Update both constants' doc comments and the compute_btc_target doc comment to record this probe (equal weights + 10m spacing + allocation_threshold 0.15). Update the compute_btc_target_* unit tests' expected values wherever the change legitimately alters them; rewrite (never delete) any test asserting reversion dominance, and add a regression test for any new behaviour.
constraints: This hypothesis modifies the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. This change MUST be made only on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch -- never as a direct commit to dev/main.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) -- only its body.
MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal's own formula or the aggregation expression; exactly one numeric constant changes (TREND 0.25 -> 1.0).

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the compute_btc_target_* unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs -- update their expected values if the new weight legitimately changes them (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, so the reviewer gives it the scrutiny an allocation-formula change deserves.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or anything on the live order-submission path.
